source_text: Crudelitas vestra gloria est nostra. Vide tantum ne hoc ipso, quod talia sustinemus, ad hoc solum videamur erumpere, ut hoc ipsum probemus, nos haec non timere, sed ultro vocare. Arrius Antoninus in Asia cum persequeretur instanter, omnes illius civitatis christiani ante tribunalia ejus se manu facta obtulerunt, cum ille, paucis duci jussis, reliquis ait, ὧ δεῖλοι, εἰ θέλετε ἀποθνήσκειν, κρημνοὺς ἢ βρόχους ἔχετε. Hoc si placuerit et hic fieri, quid facies de tantis millibus hominum, tot viris ac foeminis, omnis sexus, omnis aetatis, omnis dignitatis, offerentibus se tibi? Quantis ignibus, quantis gladiis opus erit! quid ipsa Carthago passura est, decimanda a te, cum propinquos, cum contubernales suos illic unusquisque cognoverit, cum viderit illic fortasse et tui ordinis viros et matronas, et principales quasque personas, et amicorum tuorum vel propinquos vel amicos? Parce ergo tibi, si non nobis, parce Carthagini, si non tibi, parce provinciae, quae visa intentione tua obnoxia facta est concussionibus et militum et inimicorum suorum cujusque. Magistrum neminem habemus, nisi Deum solum. Hic ante te est, nec abscondi potest, sed cui nihil facere possis. Caeterum quos putas tibi magistros, homines sunt et ipsi morituri quandoque. Nec tamen deficiet haec secta, quam tunc magis aedificari scias, cum caedi videtur. Quisque enim tantam tolerantiam spectans, ut aliquo scrupulo percussus, et inquirere accenditur, quid sit in causa, et ubi cognoverit veritatem, et ipse statim sequitur.
pass_a_gloss: Your cruelty is our glory. See to it only that by this very thing, that we endure such things, we may not seem to burst forth for this alone, that we may prove this, that we do not fear these things, but rather call for them. When Arrius Antoninus was persecuting intensely in Asia, all the Christians of that city offered themselves to him before his tribunals, since he, after ordering a few to be led away, said to the rest, 'You wretches, if you wish to die, you have cliffs or nooses.' If it pleases you for this to happen here as well, what will you do with so many thousands of people, so many men and women, of every sex, every age, every dignity, offering themselves to you? How many fires, how many swords will be needed! What will Carthage itself suffer, being decimated by you, when each person recognizes their relatives, their fellow soldiers, there, when they see perhaps even men of your own order and matrons and prominent persons and friends or relatives of your friends? Spare yourself, therefore, if not us, spare Carthage, if not yourself, spare the province, which has been made subject to extortions by your intention, both by soldiers and by its enemies. We have no master except God alone. He is before you, and cannot be hidden, but you can do nothing to Him. Moreover, those whom you think are your masters are men and will die someday. Nor will this sect fail, which you know is built up all the more when it seems to be being destroyed. For each person, seeing such great endurance, is struck by some doubt and is inspired to investigate what is the cause, and when they have learned the truth, they immediately follow.
pass_b_english: Your cruelty is our glory. Make sure it does not look as if we endure these torments only to prove a point—that we do not fear them, but actually invite them. When Arrius Antoninus was persecuting Christians hard in Asia, every Christian in that city presented themselves at his tribunal. He ordered a few of them led away, then told the rest, "You wretches, if you want to die, you have cliffs or nooses." If you want that same scene here, what will you do with thousands upon thousands of men and women, of every sex, age, and rank, offering themselves to you? How many fires, how many swords will it take? What will become of Carthage itself, decimated by you, when each person recognizes their own relatives and comrades there—perhaps even men of your own rank, noblewomen, leading citizens, and the friends or kin of your own friends? So spare yourself, if not us; spare Carthage, if not yourself; spare the province, which your policy has already handed over to extortion by soldiers and by every man's enemies alike. We have no master but God alone. He stands before you; He cannot be hidden, yet you can do nothing to Him. As for those you take for masters, they are mere men who will die someday. Still this sect will not fail—you can see it grows stronger precisely when it seems to be cut down. For anyone who witnesses such endurance feels a stab of doubt, begins to ask what drives it, and once they grasp the truth, they follow it at once.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The Greek phrase 'ὧ δεῖλοι, εἰ θέλετε ἀποθνήσκειν, κρημνοὺς ἢ βρόχους ἔχετε' is correctly translated in both as 'You wretches, if you wish to die, you have cliffs or nooses.' The nuances of 'concussionibus' (extortions) and 'caeterum' (moreover/as for) are handled correctly. The title 'Persecution is Our Glory' accurately reflects the opening sentiment 'Crudelitas vestra gloria est nostra'.

The Latin text is correctly identified as 'To Scapula 5' from the specified edition. The translation accurately reflects the source text, preserving all arguments, quotations, and meanings.
